result.content:
VERDICT: Proceed with log-only diagnostics: add forecast-error-by-lead-time cross-check against cal_err failures and per-hour calibration violation listing before any blending changes; no promotion-bar relaxation.

REASONING: Tree is settle_hour-only, so any skill/blend signal varying by lead time or hour is invisible to the current model and can only be validated diagnostically first. Cross-referencing model_skill error buckets with calibration error (cal_err) failures isolates whether miscalibration is a skill problem (fix in blend) or a binning problem (fix in calibration layer). Listing the worst-violating hours gives a concrete, ranked target set for future settle_hour-conditional adjustments without touching promotion criteria. hourly_wx_axes and model_break_decay should stay gated until their graduation criteria are met; diagnostics now will provide that evidence.

NEXT_STEPS:
1. In model_skill.py, add a grouped metric: forecast error (e.g., MAE/log-loss) bucketed by lead_time_hours alongside the existing skill aggregate; emit as log-only output from the existing skill computation function (no change to return values used downstream).
2. In the calibration path (cal_err computation site), join cal_err failures to the lead-time buckets from step 1 by (settle_hour, lead_time) key; log a contingency summary flagging buckets where high skill error coincides with calibration failure.
3. Add a diagnostic listing function that ranks settle_hours by |predicted_prob − empirical_freq| within each calibration bin; log top-N violating hours with sample counts (suppress hours below a min-sample threshold to avoid noise).
4. In model_blend_*.py, verify blend weights remain static; add an assertion/log warning if any weight path reads lead-time or hour features (guarding against silent scope creep beyond settle_hour).
5. Add an autopilot evidence hook: persist the per-hour violation table so hourly_wx_axes / model_break_decay graduation checks can consume it once their existing criteria trigger.

CALL_BACK_IF: Any lead-time bucket shows calibration failure with adequate skill (i.e., miscalibration not explained by forecast error), or top violating hours persist across ≥2 evaluation windows — then propose a scoped settle_hour-conditional calibration fix.
